name: Zimran
overview: Zimran was a male figure in the Bible, known primarily as a son of Abraham through his wife Keturah. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or personal characteristics. His mention is brief and focused on his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Zimran appears as a proper name in Genesis 25:2. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is recorded in Scripture, and thus it is presented plainly without further significance.
familyAndRelationships: Zimran is identified as a son of Abraham, the patriarch, and Keturah, his wife after Sarah's death. These relationships are explicitly noted in Genesis 25:2. No other family relationships are recorded for him in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Zimran's significance lies in his role as one of the sons Abraham fathered through Keturah, highlighting Abraham's expanded lineage beyond Isaac. This contributes to the biblical record of Abraham's descendants and God's covenantal blessings extended through him. Though not central to the primary covenant line, Zimran represents the broader fulfillment of God's promise to make Abraham a father of many nations.
